A practical option for extensions, repairs and infill on red brick streets across the capital and beyond.

name: Milton Red Multi
description: Milton Red Multi takes the warmth of the standard Milton Red and adds darker and lighter tones across each face, so a finished wall picks up noticeably more depth. The variation suits larger elevations where a single flat colour can look monotonous, and works equally well on a smaller extension needing character.

name: Orient Red Multi
description: Orient Red Multi mixes warm reds with orange and darker brown tones across each face, so the brickwork gains a rich, layered appearance. The warmth lifts noticeably in low sun, which is why it is a good choice for elevations that catch morning or evening light. It suits housing, garden walls and infill work where a warmer, livelier red is preferred to a flat one.

name: New Buxton Red
description: New Buxton Red is a solid, honest red with a softly grained face and quiet tonal movement, offering warmth without fuss. It performs well across whole elevations as well as smaller extensions and garden walls, and pairs easily with grey or buff mortar depending on the effect you want.

name: Richmond Smoked Red
description: Richmond Smoked Red carries a warm red body overlaid with smoky, darker patches, which leaves elevations with the softened, slightly sooty character of older urban walls. The effect adds depth and age without going as far as a full antique brick. Well suited to period extensions, infill and feature elevations in a 65mm metric format.

name: Lambourne Mixture
description: Lambourne Mixture blends reds, browns and softer buff tones into brickwork with the easy, unforced variation of an older wall. The mixture reads warm overall while individual bricks range widely, which gives elevations depth without demanding attention. A comfortable choice for extensions, rural housing and garden structures. The lightly textured face adds a further layer of interest across larger areas of brickwork.

name: Malvern Village Mixture
description: Malvern Village Mixture is built around the gentle, weathered variety of English village brickwork, mixing warm reds and browns with softer, lighter bricks throughout. The result feels settled and rural rather than newly built. A natural fit for cottage extensions, village infill and conservation area work in a standard 65mm format.

name: Grosvenor Handmade
description: A handmade brick with the creased, sand-moulded face and softly irregular edges that come only from hand production. Colours run through warm reds and browns with natural variation between bricks, so walls build up with genuine character. Suited to period restoration, conservation work, high-end housing and feature elevations in a 65mm metric format.

name: New Leighton Blend
description: New Leighton Blend brings together reds, browns and lighter buff tones with a softly grained face, which gives brickwork balanced variation that works at any scale. The blend is warm without being strong, so it becomes straightforward to match with existing materials on extensions and infill projects.

name: Garrigue Grey
description: Garrigue Grey is a soft, muted grey with gentle tonal movement, avoiding both the flatness of a uniform grey and the harshness of a charcoal. Grey brickwork has become a mainstay of contemporary residential design, working particularly well with dark frames, glazing and timber cladding. A dependable choice for contemporary housing, extensions and feature elevations where a softer grey is wanted.

name: Milton Red
description: Milton Red is a clean, even red with a faintly textured face and restrained variation, giving elevations warmth and consistency in equal measure. It is the kind of brick that does not fight with anything else on a building, and that makes it useful for housing, extensions and boundary walls alike.

name: Alderley Russet Blend
description: Alderley Russet Blend runs through russet reds, warm browns and softer orange tones, lending walls an autumnal depth that reads rich without becoming dark. The blend suits both traditional and contemporary settings, and works particularly well on elevations that catch low morning or evening light.

name: Cooksbridge Yellow Clamp Stock
description: A clamp-fired yellow stock brick, carrying the smoky discolouration, uneven colour and creased face that clamp firing produces. Colours run from soft yellow through to darker scorched patches, which leaves elevations with the genuine irregularity of historic stock walls. A strong choice for conservation work, period extensions and infill in stock brick areas.

name: Manorial Red
description: Manorial Red offers the warmth of the Manorial family in a more consistent red, with a gently worked surface and modest variation across each brick. It gives elevations an even, dignified appearance without tipping into uniformity, and suits housing, extensions and boundary walls. The result is warm and dependable without demanding any particular treatment or detailing.

name: Hamsey Mixed Stock
description: Hamsey Mixed Stock brings together yellows, buffs and darker scorched bricks in the manner of a traditional stock wall, with creased faces and irregular arrises throughout. The mix reads as weathered and established rather than newly built, making it a natural fit for conservation work, period extensions and sensitive infill projects.

name: Bexhill Purple Multi
description: Bexhill Purple Multi carries purple and plum tones blended with reds and browns, which gives brickwork a distinctive cool depth that sets it apart from a conventional red multi. The colouring suits both period matching, where purple bricks are common in older walls, and contemporary schemes looking for something less predictable.

name: Bexhill Red
description: Bexhill Red is a warm, softly varied red with a lightly weathered face, sitting comfortably between a clean modern facing brick and a full antique. It is a versatile choice for extensions, housing and garden walls, and pairs easily with the darker and purple options in the same range for added depth.

name: Birtley Olde English
description: Birtley Olde English blends warm reds and browns with a softly textured, irregular face to give brickwork an unmistakably traditional character. It builds into walls with plenty of tonal movement, which suits period extensions, cottages and rural projects particularly well.

name: Coleridge Yellow Multi
description: Coleridge Yellow Multi blends warm yellows with buff and softer brown tones, so the brickwork gains the golden, varied appearance associated with older yellow stock walls. It brings brightness to an elevation while keeping enough movement to look established rather than new. It works well on extensions, infill and garden walls in yellow brick areas.

name: Crowborough Multi
description: Crowborough Multi mixes reds and browns with darker mottling across each face, which produces walls with warmth and quiet depth. The variation is enough to give large elevations interest without ever becoming the focus, which is why it is a sound choice for housing, extensions and boundary walls in a 65mm metric format.

name: Hardwicke Sherwood Blaze
description: Hardwicke Sherwood Blaze lives up to its name with warm orange-red tones and bright flashes across the face, so a finished wall picks up genuine energy in sunlight. The livelier colouring suits elevations that need lifting, and works well as a contrast against darker brick, timber or grey render.

name: Chailey Medium Multi
description: Chailey Medium Multi blends reds, browns and softer tones at a medium depth, so elevations come out with balanced variation that neither disappears nor dominates. The medium register makes it one of the easier bricks to match into existing walls, which is why it appears so often on extensions and repair work in Sussex and beyond.

name: Cheddar Golden
description: Cheddar Golden is a warm honey-buff brick with gentle variation, bringing brightness and a soft glow to elevations without the starkness of a pale grey or white. It works particularly well where brickwork needs to sit alongside stone or render, and holds its warmth well in low afternoon light.

name: Brunswick Red
description: Brunswick Red is a clean, warm red with a faintly textured face and restrained tonal variation, giving elevations consistency without looking manufactured. It is an easy brick to specify across whole houses, extensions and garden walls, and takes either a grey or buff mortar comfortably depending on the effect you are after.

name: New Chailey Stock
description: New Chailey Stock offers the creased, weathered face and varied yellow-to-brown colouring of a traditional Sussex stock brick, newly manufactured for consistent sizing and supply. It builds into walls with genuine character and irregularity, suiting period extensions, garden walls and conservation area work. The creased faces and softened arrises are what give the finished wall its convincing irregularity.

name: Birtley Olde English Buff
description: The buff version of Birtley Olde English, swapping warm reds for soft sandy and cream tones while keeping the same textured, irregular face. The result is traditional brickwork with a lighter, brighter presence, aimed squarely at period extensions and rural work in areas where buff and stone predominate rather than red brick.

name: Cheddar Red
description: Cheddar Red completes the Cheddar range with a warm, softly varied red and a softly grained face. It is a straightforward and dependable facing brick, suited to new build housing, extensions and boundary walls, and easily blended with the Brown and Golden options for additional depth.

name: Cottage Mixture
description: Cottage Mixture is exactly what the name suggests: a soft, varied blend of reds, browns and lighter tones with an irregular face, echoing the modest brickwork of rural cottages. It builds into walls that look unplanned and settled rather than specified. A natural choice for cottage extensions, village infill and garden structures.

name: Hardwicke Welbeck Autumn Antique
description: Hardwicke Welbeck Autumn Antique combines autumnal reds, oranges and browns with a deliberately aged, weathered face, so brickwork reads as long established rather than newly laid. It is at home on period extensions, conservation work and rural projects where a fresh brick would sit awkwardly against older walls. The colouring stays warm throughout, so the wall reads mellow rather than sooty.

name: Brunswick Antique Red
description: Brunswick Antique Red carries a warm red body overlaid with darkened, weathered patches and a softly worn face, so brickwork looks established from the moment it is pointed. It is aimed at period extensions, restoration work and any project where a crisp new brick would look conspicuous alongside older walls.

name: Cheddar Brown
description: Cheddar Brown is a warm mid-brown with soft tonal movement across the face, offering an alternative to red and buff that sits comfortably against timber, stone and dark frames. Brown brickwork reads as understated and natural rather than assertive, and the result is a quietly versatile choice for housing and extensions.

name: Calderstone Russet
description: Calderstone Russet combines warm russet reds and browns with a gently worked face, so the wall reads as with autumnal warmth and quiet variation. It is an unshowy brick that works across whole elevations as readily as on a single extension, and pairs comfortably with buff or grey mortar depending on the effect wanted.

name: Manorial Mixture
description: Manorial Mixture blends warm reds, browns and softer weathered tones into brickwork with the settled, generous character its name suggests. The variation is broad enough to feel genuinely traditional, and that makes it a natural fit for period extensions, country houses and conservation area work in a standard 65mm format. The lightly textured face adds a further layer of depth once the brickwork is pointed.

name: Cavendish Dorket Honeygold
description: Dorket Honeygold is one of the more recognisable golden bricks in UK housebuilding, with a warm honey body lifted by lighter flecks and gentle mottling. It brings a soft, mellow quality to elevations and photographs particularly well in evening light. Suited to new build housing and extensions alike where warmth is wanted without going full red.

name: Etruria Mixture
description: Etruria Mixture blends deep reds, browns and darker tones into brickwork with weight and character, drawing on the hard, richly coloured clays associated with the Staffordshire potteries. The mixture reads solid and traditional, making it a good fit for period work, urban infill and elevations needing presence.

name: Grampian Red Mixture
description: Grampian Red Mixture blends warm reds with darker browns and occasional lighter bricks, giving elevations depth and a hard-wearing, northern character. The mixture is broad enough to add real interest and consistent enough to specify confidently across a whole house or a large development.

name: Leicester Grey
description: Leicester Grey is a soft mid-grey with gentle variation across the face, offering a contemporary alternative to the reds and buffs of the wider Leicester range. It works well on modern housing, extensions and feature elevations, and pairs particularly effectively with dark window frames and timber.

name: Bradgate Claret
description: Bradgate Claret is a deep wine-red brick with purple undertones, giving elevations a richer and more formal character than a conventional red. The darker body holds its presence across large areas, which suits urban housing, apartment schemes and elevations wanting a more considered palette.

name: Bradgate Medium Grey
description: Bradgate Medium Grey is a balanced mid-grey with soft tonal movement across the face, avoiding both the flatness of a uniform grey and the severity of a charcoal. It gives contemporary elevations a calm, even surface, and pairs particularly well with dark window frames, glazing and timber cladding.

name: Bradgate Regal
description: Bradgate Regal is a richer, deeper brick with darker tones running through a warm red base, so a finished wall picks up a formal presence that suits larger and more prominent elevations. The name fits: this is a brick with weight to it, a sound choice for apartment schemes, civic work and houses wanting a considered palette.

name: Thakeham Red Multi
description: Thakeham Red Multi blends warm reds with browns and darker mottling across each face, which produces walls with depth and a comfortable, lived-in quality. The variation reads well at both close range and across a full elevation, making it a versatile option for housing, extensions and boundary walls.

name: Arden Weathered Grey
description: Arden Weathered Grey takes the same mid-grey body and adds darkened, uneven weathering across the face, leaving brickwork with considerably more depth and age than a uniform grey. The effect suits contemporary buildings wanting texture and older properties needing a grey that does not look brand new.

name: Rosa Blanca
description: Rosa Blanca is a pale brick with a soft rose-tinted white body, giving elevations a light, delicate quality that sits between a cream and a very light red. The subtlety suits contemporary architecture and schemes where brickwork is meant to recede rather than dominate.

name: Leicester Weathered Red
description: Leicester Weathered Red pairs a consistent warm red with a darkened, softly weathered face, so brickwork looks settled without the strong colour variation of a multi. It suits extensions, repairs and garden walls where an aged appearance is wanted alongside an even overall tone.

name: New Ivanhoe Cream
description: New Ivanhoe Cream is a soft, pale cream brick with gentle variation, bringing lightness and warmth to elevations without the coldness of a grey or the flatness of a white. It works particularly well on contemporary housing and in areas where stone and render predominate over red brick.

name: Bradgate Golden Purple
description: Bradgate Golden Purple is an unusual and striking combination, pairing golden and buff tones with purple and plum mottling across the same face. The result gives brickwork genuine complexity, catching light in a way that flatter bricks cannot, and works well as a feature elevation or a whole-house brick with character.

name: Laybrook Yellow
description: Laybrook Yellow is a soft, warm yellow brick with gentle variation, bringing the traditional brightness of English yellow brickwork to new elevations. It sits comfortably alongside genuine stock brick without pretending to be reclaimed, and that makes it a straightforward choice for extensions and infill in yellow brick areas.

name: Grosvenor Autumn Flame
description: Grosvenor Autumn Flame combines warm reds with orange and amber flashes across the face, which gives brickwork genuine energy in sunlight. The livelier colouring lifts elevations that might otherwise feel flat, and works especially well on walls catching morning or evening light. It also works effectively as a contrast band against grey, buff or darker brickwork.

name: Dorset Red
description: Dorset Red is a warm, mellow red with soft variation and a faintly textured face, carrying the gentler colouring associated with south west brickwork rather than a hard industrial red. It suits period extensions, rural housing and garden walls where warmth matters more than uniformity.

name: Arden Grey
description: Arden Grey is a clean mid-grey with subtle tonal movement, giving contemporary elevations a calm, even surface without looking manufactured. Grey brickwork pairs particularly well with dark frames, glazing, zinc and timber cladding, which has made it a mainstay of modern residential design.

name: Leicester Multi Yellow
description: Leicester Multi Yellow blends warm yellows with buff and softer brown tones, producing brightness with enough variation to look established rather than new. Yellow brickwork carries a distinctly traditional English character, and this one works well on extensions and infill in yellow brick areas.

name: Ivanhoe Westminster
description: Ivanhoe Westminster is a refined brick with soft tonal variation and a subtly textured surface, aiming for the composed, slightly formal appearance associated with better quality urban brickwork. It suits city extensions, apartment schemes and elevations where a considered rather than rustic finish is wanted.

name: Hardwicke Welbeck Red Mixture
description: Hardwicke Welbeck Red Mixture blends warm reds and browns with gentle variation and a face that carries a light grain, which gives brickwork depth without heavy weathering. It is a versatile, dependable brick suited to extensions, boundary walls and whole elevations, and blends readily with the Autumn Antique from the same range.

name: Bradgate Red
description: Bradgate Red is a clean, warm red with a softly grained face and restrained variation, giving elevations consistency and warmth in equal measure. It is a straightforward brick to specify across whole houses, extensions and garden walls, and forms the natural starting point of the wider Bradgate range.

name: Leicester Red Stock
description: Leicester Red Stock offers the creased face and softened arrises of traditional stock brick production in a consistent warm red. The texture gives brickwork character while the steadier colour keeps elevations even, so it becomes a practical middle ground between a plain facing brick and a full multi.

name: Ivanhoe Cream Original
description: Ivanhoe Cream Original is a soft, pale cream brick with gentle variation and a faintly grained face, bringing brightness and warmth to elevations without the coldness of grey or the flatness of white. It works particularly well in areas where stone and render predominate over red brick.

name: Leicester Orange
description: Leicester Orange is a warm terracotta-toned brick with soft variation, brighter and sunnier than a conventional red without becoming garish. The orange lifts noticeably in low sun, which is why it is a good choice for elevations that catch morning or evening light, as well as for contrast banding.

name: Capital Brown Multi
description: Capital Brown Multi blends warm browns with darker and lighter tones, lending walls an understated depth that works particularly well on larger urban elevations. Brown reads as more neutral than red and warmer than grey, and the result is a useful middle ground on commercial and residential schemes alike.

name: Leicester Multi Red Stock
description: Leicester Multi Red Stock combines the creased, weathered face of a stock brick with a multi-toned red body, so the brickwork gains both texture and colour variation. The result feels traditional and hard-working, suiting period extensions, infill and garden walls.

name: Leicester Weathered Multi
description: Leicester Weathered Multi combines multi-toned reds and browns with a weathered, darkened face, which leaves elevations with the appearance of a wall that has stood for decades. It is a useful choice for extensions and repairs where new brickwork needs to blend rather than announce itself.

name: Heritage Red Blend
description: Heritage Red Blend mixes warm reds, browns and softer weathered tones into brickwork with the varied, unforced appearance of an older wall. The blend is aimed squarely at sensitive work, where a single flat colour would look wrong against a period elevation, and works equally well on rural infill.

name: New Cavendish Stock
description: New Cavendish Stock offers the varied colouring and creased, irregular face of a traditional stock brick, running through soft yellows, buffs and darker scorched tones. It builds into walls with genuine character, making it aimed squarely at period extensions, garden walls and conservation area work in a 65mm metric format.

name: Marlborough Stock
description: Marlborough Stock carries the creased face, softened arrises and varied colouring of a traditional stock brick, newly manufactured for consistent sizing and reliable supply. Tones run through warm buffs and browns with darker patches throughout, lending walls the weathered character of an established wall.

name: Oatmeal Textured
description: Oatmeal Textured is a soft, neutral brick in the pale oatmeal and light buff range, finished with a fine surface texture that gives quiet depth without pattern. It is a restrained, easy brick to build with, sitting comfortably alongside render, timber, stone and glazing on contemporary and traditional work alike.

name: Abingworth Red Multi
description: Abingworth Red Multi blends warm reds with browns and darker mottling across each face, which leaves elevations with depth that reads well both close up and across a full elevation. It is a versatile, unshowy multi suited to housing, extensions and boundary walls. The lightly textured face adds a further layer of depth once the brickwork is pointed.

name: Sandalwood
description: Sandalwood is a warm, soft brick in the sandy buff to light brown range, with gentle variation that keeps larger elevations from flattening out. The neutral warmth makes it genuinely versatile, working as comfortably on a contemporary house as on a traditional extension.

name: Swanbourne Yellow Multi
description: Swanbourne Yellow Multi blends warm yellows with buff and softer brown tones, giving brightness to an elevation while keeping enough movement to look established rather than newly built. Yellow brickwork carries a distinctly traditional English character, and this one suits extensions and infill in yellow brick areas.

name: Tradesman Light
description: Tradesman Light is a pale, softly varied brick in the light buff and cream range, bringing brightness to elevations without the starkness of a white or the coolness of a grey. It is an easy brick to build with and pairs readily with render, stone and timber on contemporary and traditional work alike.

name: Tyneham Restoration Red
description: Tyneham Restoration Red is built for matching work. The mellow red body, uneven face and gentle weathering are all aimed at blending new brickwork into old rather than standing out as a modern insertion. It comes in two heights, and picking the right one matters more here than on most bricks, since the whole point is to vanish into an existing wall rather than sit proud of its coursing.

name: Berry Light Stock
description: Berry Light Stock pairs the creased, irregular face of a traditional stock brick with a lighter overall colouring, running through pale buffs and soft yellows with occasional darker bricks. The lighter palette brightens elevations while the stock character keeps them from looking new, a useful combination on period extensions.

name: Tradesman Millgate Buff
description: Tradesman Millgate Buff is a soft sandy buff with gentle tonal movement and a subtly textured surface, offering brightness with a hint of industrial character. It works well on contemporary housing, conversions and extensions where a pale brick is wanted but a flat modern finish would feel wrong.

name: Tradesman Antique Grey
description: Tradesman Antique Grey combines a soft grey body with darkened, uneven weathering, so the brickwork gains the aged appearance of grey walls that have stood for decades. The result is far less clinical than a uniform modern grey, and the result is useful where a contemporary colour needs to sit alongside older buildings.

name: New Sandhurst Stock
description: New Sandhurst Stock combines the creased face and softened edges of traditional stock production with warm sandy and buff colouring throughout. The result is brickwork with an established, weathered quality straight off the pallet, suiting period extensions, infill and garden walls in stock brick areas.

name: Grainger Autumn
description: Grainger Autumn blends warm reds, oranges and browns into brickwork with an autumnal richness, lighter and livelier than the Antique from the same range. The warmth lifts noticeably in low sun, making it a good choice for elevations that catch morning or evening light. It also works well as a warmer contrast against grey or buff brickwork.

name: Audley Red Mixture
description: Audley Red Mixture brings together warm reds, browns and softer tones with a gently worked surface, so elevations come out with the easy variation of an older wall. The mixture reads warm overall while individual bricks range widely, giving elevations depth without demanding attention.

name: Tradesman Heather
description: Tradesman Heather blends purple, brown and red tones across a face that carries a light grain, which leaves elevations with a soft, heathered depth that works as well on a whole house as on a single extension. It is a versatile, unshowy brick that sits comfortably in most settings.

name: Tradesman Rustic
description: Tradesman Rustic pairs a warm red body with a textured, roughened face that gives brickwork shadow and depth across an elevation. The rustic finish reads traditional without tipping into antique, making it a practical middle ground for housing, extensions and boundary walls in the standard 65mm format. The warm red colouring stays consistent, so the interest comes from the surface rather than tonal variation.

name: Hatton Multi
description: Hatton Multi blends warm reds and browns with lighter and darker bricks running through, giving elevations balanced tonal movement. It is a dependable everyday multi that works as readily on a new build estate as on a single rear extension, and takes either grey or buff mortar comfortably.

name: Tradesman Sandfaced Red Multi
description: Tradesman Sandfaced Red Multi combines multi-toned reds with a fine sand-textured face, leaving brickwork that looks matt and traditional rather than sharp and modern. The sand softens the colour slightly, which helps new work sit comfortably alongside older brickwork on extensions and repairs.

name: Grainger Antique
description: Grainger Antique carries darkened, uneven weathering across a worn, irregular face, so brickwork reads as long established from the day it is pointed. Colours sit through reds and browns with patchy darker areas throughout. A strong candidate for period extensions, restoration and barn conversions in the standard 65mm format. A soft lime-toned mortar will reinforce the aged appearance considerably.

name: Ivanhoe Olde Village
description: Ivanhoe Olde Village blends warm reds and browns with softer weathered tones and an irregular face, so the brickwork gains the settled, unplanned character of village walls. It builds up with genuine variation, so it becomes a natural fit for cottage extensions, rural infill and conservation area work.

name: Tradesman Light Rustic Blend
description: Tradesman Light Rustic Blend pairs pale buff and cream tones with a textured, roughened face, lending walls brightness and surface depth at once. The rustic finish stops the light colouring from reading as flat, and that makes it a useful choice for extensions, garden walls and rural projects.

name: Mixed Buff Rustic
description: Mixed Buff Rustic combines pale sandy and cream tones with a textured, roughened face, which gives brickwork brightness and surface interest at the same time. The rustic finish stops the pale colouring from reading as flat, which is why it is a useful option for extensions, garden walls and rural work.

name: Tyneham Blend
description: Tyneham Blend brings together reds, browns and softer weathered tones with an irregular face, so a finished wall picks up the varied appearance of a wall that has stood for generations. The wider palette suits period extensions and rural work where a single flat colour would look wrong against older brickwork.

name: Weston Red Multi
description: Weston Red Multi runs through warm reds with browns and darker mottling mixed across each face, so the wall reads as with genuine depth over larger areas. It is a straightforward, reliable multi that suits new build anything from a rear extension to a full elevation without needing any particular treatment or detailing.

name: Tradesman Buff Multi
description: Tradesman Buff Multi blends pale sandy buffs with warmer cream and light brown tones, giving brightness to an elevation while keeping enough variation to avoid looking flat. It sits comfortably with render, stone and timber, making it a practical choice for both contemporary and traditional schemes.

name: Grantchester Blend
description: Grantchester Blend brings together soft reds, buffs and gentle brown tones with a lightly weathered face, which gives brickwork the understated variation of an older wall. The blend is restrained rather than dramatic, so it becomes easy to pair with existing materials on extensions and infill work.

name: Keswick Blend Brick Slip
description: Keswick Blend as a brick slip brings a warm, varied mix of reds and browns to internal walls and cladding systems, with a face carrying enough irregularity to read as genuine brickwork rather than a veneer. Useful for feature walls, chimney breasts and retrofit insulation systems where depth is limited.

name: Audley Antique Brick Slip
description: Audley Antique in brick slip form gives you the same weathered, aged face as the full brick at a fraction of the depth. Slips are cut thin so they can be bonded to internal walls, feature chimney breasts, insulated cladding systems and anywhere a full brick skin is not practical. Ideal for retrofit and fit-out projects needing genuine fired clay.

name: Old Coach House
description: Old Coach House carries the worn, darkened character of outbuilding brickwork that has weathered for a century or more, with reds and browns overlaid by patchy aged tones and an irregular face. It is a natural fit for barn conversions, period extensions and garden structures where a fresh brick would look conspicuous.

name: Birkdale Blend Brick Slip
description: Birkdale Blend in slip form offers softly blended reds and browns with a lightly weathered face, giving interior brickwork warmth and depth without the thickness of a full brick. Well suited to feature walls, chimney breasts, kitchen and retail fit-outs, and insulated cladding systems on retrofit projects. Corner slips are needed at external angles to keep the effect convincing.

name: Shelford Cream Multi
description: Shelford Cream Multi blends soft creams with pale buff and light brown tones, giving elevations brightness with enough variation to avoid looking flat. The gentle palette sits comfortably with render, stone, timber and glazing, making it useful on contemporary and traditional schemes alike. It suits new build housing, extensions and boundary walls equally well.

name: Olde English Red Multi
description: Olde English Red Multi blends warm reds and browns over a softly irregular, lightly weathered face, lending walls the unforced variation of an older wall. It builds up with genuine tonal movement, making it a natural fit for period extensions, cottages and rural infill in the standard 65mm format. A soft lime-toned mortar will reinforce the traditional appearance considerably.

name: London Weathered Yellow Brick Slip
description: London Weathered Yellow in slip form captures the smoky, discoloured yellow of the capital's stock brickwork, in a thin format for internal walls and cladding. Colours run from soft yellow to noticeably darkened, with creased faces throughout, giving interiors the character of a genuine London wall. Corner slips are needed at external angles, so allow for these when calculating quantities.

name: Middleton Blend
description: Middleton Blend mixes warm reds and browns with softer neutral tones and a softly grained face, so the brickwork gains balanced variation that works comfortably at any scale. It is an easy blend to specify, adding depth to large elevations without becoming the dominant feature of a building.

name: Olde English Buff Multi
description: Olde English Buff Multi blends pale sandy buffs with warmer cream and light brown tones over a softly irregular face, which leaves elevations with brightness and traditional character at once. It works particularly well on period extensions and rural projects in areas where buff and stone predominate rather than red brick.

name: Audley Antique
description: Audley Antique carries darkened, patchy weathering across a worn and irregular face, so new brickwork reads as long established rather than freshly laid. Colours run through warm reds and browns with softer aged tones throughout, making it a natural choice for period extensions, conservation work and barn conversions.

name: Kimpton Blend
description: Kimpton Blend mixes warm reds, browns and softer neutral tones with a faintly textured face, which produces walls with balanced variation that works at any scale. It is a quietly versatile blend, easy to specify across a whole house and easy to match against existing materials on smaller extensions.

name: Hemmingstone Antique
description: Hemmingstone Antique carries the darkened, softened tones and irregular face of brickwork that has stood for generations. Reds and browns are overlaid with weathered patches, so walls read as established from the day they are finished. A soft lime-toned mortar will reinforce the aged appearance considerably.

name: Traditional Red Blend
description: Traditional Red Blend mixes warm reds and browns with a lightly weathered, irregular face, so a finished wall picks up the settled character of an established wall. It is a dependable choice for period extensions, repairs and infill work where a crisp modern brick would sit awkwardly against older brickwork.

name: Maranello
description: Maranello is a rich, saturated red with depth and warmth, named for a place synonymous with a particular shade of it. The strong colouring gives elevations real presence, working well on feature walls and contemporary houses where the brickwork is intended to be the boldest element.

name: Reclaimed Mixture
description: Reclaimed Mixture is made to look as though it has already been salvaged from an old wall, mixing worn reds and browns with darker weathered bricks and irregular faces throughout. It offers the character of genuine reclaims with the consistent sizing and reliable availability that reclaimed stock cannot.

name: Barnhouse Blend Brick Slip
description: Barnhouse Blend as a brick slip brings the warm, varied reds and browns of rural barn brickwork to internal walls and cladding systems. The blended colouring and worn face give feature walls genuine agricultural character, and at slip depth it works where a full brick skin would be impossible. Well suited to feature walls, chimney breasts, retail fit-outs and retrofit insulation systems.

name: Normandy Grey
description: Normandy Grey is a soft, slightly weathered grey with gentle tonal movement, avoiding the flatness of a uniform modern grey. The muted colouring reads as European and understated rather than starkly contemporary, which is why it is easy to pair with timber, stone and off-white render. It suits contemporary housing, extensions and elevations wanting a softer grey than a charcoal.

name: Waveney Red Blend
description: Waveney Red Blend brings together warm reds and softer brown tones over a softly grained face, so elevations come out with quiet depth and an East Anglian gentleness rather than a hard industrial red. It suits period extensions, rural housing and garden walls.

name: Euphoria
description: Euphoria is a distinctive brick with rich, layered colouring that shifts between warm and darker tones across each face, giving elevations real complexity. It is a brick chosen for effect rather than neutrality, working well on feature walls and contemporary houses where the brickwork is meant to be noticed.

name: Tradesman Tudor Regent
description: Tradesman Tudor Regent brings deep reds and browns together with dark mottling and a lightly rustic face, so a finished wall picks up the warm, aged depth associated with traditional Tudor-style walls. It suits period extensions, garden walls and elevations wanting character without heavy weathering.

name: London Weathered Yellow
description: London Weathered Yellow captures the smoky, discoloured yellow of stock brickwork across the capital, where soot and time have darkened an originally pale brick. Colours run from soft yellow to noticeably dark, with a creased, irregular face throughout. A strong choice for conservation work and extensions in stock brick streets.

name: Mystique
description: Mystique is a darker, more atmospheric brick with deep tones shifting across each face, giving elevations depth that flatter bricks cannot match. It suits contemporary architecture and feature walls where the brickwork is meant to hold attention, and works powerfully against glazing, timber and pale render.

name: Lava
description: Lava is a dark, dramatic brick in the deep charcoal to near-black range, with surface movement that stops large elevations reading as flat. Dark brickwork has become a signature of contemporary architecture, working powerfully against glazing, timber and pale render. It suits contemporary housing, feature elevations and schemes built around strong contrast.

name: Fine Handmade Textured Red Blend
description: A genuine handmade brick, sand moulded so each face carries the creases, folds and softly irregular edges that only hand production gives. The blended red colouring adds further variation on top of the surface character. Suited to period restoration, conservation work and high-end residential projects where uniformity would be a drawback.

name: Mystique Brick Slip
description: Mystique in slip form brings the same dark, atmospheric colouring to internal walls and cladding systems, with tones shifting across each face to give real depth. It suits contemporary interiors, feature walls and commercial fit-outs where dark brickwork is wanted without the thickness of a full skin. Corner slips are needed at external angles to keep the effect convincing.

name: Rothesay Blend
description: Rothesay Blend mixes warm reds and browns with softer neutral tones over a subtly textured surface, so the wall reads as with quiet, balanced variation. It is an easy blend to build with, adding depth to elevations without demanding attention or dictating the rest of the material palette.

name: Sahara Buff
description: Sahara Buff is a light, sun-bleached brick in the pale sandy range, with soft variation that keeps larger areas from flattening out. The bright, warm colouring suits contemporary builds particularly well and pairs effectively with timber, render and dark window frames. It works particularly well on contemporary housing, extensions and boundary walls.

name: Old Coach House Brick Slip
description: Old Coach House as a brick slip brings the worn, darkened character of century-old outbuilding brickwork to interior walls and cladding systems. Reds and browns are overlaid with patchy aged tones and irregular faces, giving feature walls and conversions genuine period atmosphere at slip depth. Well suited to feature walls, chimney breasts, barn conversions and retrofit insulation systems.

name: Hathaway Brindled
description: Hathaway Brindled carries the streaked, mottled colouring that brindling produces, with darker tones running across a warm red-brown base. The effect gives brickwork genuine surface interest and a traditional, hard-wearing character, at home on period extensions and elevations wanting depth without heavy weathering.

name: Crofters Medley
description: Crofters Medley mixes warm reds, browns and softer weathered tones with an irregular face, so a finished wall picks up the unplanned, hard-working character of rural cottage walls. The wide blend builds up with genuine variation, making it a natural fit for cottage extensions, village infill and garden structures.

name: Kempley Antique
description: Kempley Antique carries darkened, patchy weathering across a worn and irregular face, so new brickwork reads as long established rather than freshly laid. Colours run through warm reds and browns with softer aged tones throughout, making it a natural choice for period extensions and conservation work.

name: Olde Essex Red Multi
description: Olde Essex Red Multi blends warm reds and browns over a softly irregular face, which leaves elevations with the traditional variation associated with older Essex and East Anglian walls. It builds up with genuine tonal movement, suiting period extensions, rural infill and garden structures in the standard 65mm format. A soft lime-toned mortar will reinforce the traditional appearance considerably.

name: Oakwood Multi
description: Oakwood Multi blends warm browns and reds with softer neutral tones, so the brickwork gains an understated, natural depth that pairs particularly well with timber and stone. Brown reads as more neutral than red and warmer than grey, making this a useful middle ground on both residential and commercial work.

name: Kassandra Multi
description: Kassandra Multi blends warm reds and browns with lighter and darker tones across each face, which gives brickwork depth and a hint of Mediterranean warmth. The variation reads well both close up and across a full elevation, making it a versatile option for housing, extensions and boundary walls.

name: Medium Surrey Blend
description: Medium Surrey Blend brings together reds, browns and softer tones at a medium depth, so the brickwork gains balanced variation in the manner of traditional Surrey and Home Counties walls. The medium register makes it one of the easier bricks to match into existing brickwork on extensions and repair work.

name: Corn Yellow
description: Corn Yellow is a warm golden-yellow brick with soft variation, bringing genuine brightness to elevations without tipping into a harsh primary colour. The golden tone lifts noticeably in low sun, and the result is particularly effective on walls catching morning or evening light. It suits housing, garden walls and infill work, and works well as a warm contrast against grey brickwork.

name: Pagus Grey Black
description: Pagus Grey Black sits between charcoal and black, with tonal shifts across the face that stop large elevations reading as flat. The dark colouring gives contemporary architecture real presence and works powerfully against glazing, timber cladding and pale render. It suits contemporary housing, feature elevations and schemes built around strong contrast.

name: Peak Bordeaux
description: Peak Bordeaux is a deep wine-red brick with purple undertones, giving elevations a richer and more formal presence than a conventional red. The darker body holds up well across large areas, which suits apartment schemes, urban housing and elevations wanting a more considered palette.

name: Dartmoor Heather
description: Dartmoor Heather blends purple, brown and red tones across a face that carries a light grain, which gives brickwork the soft heathered depth of moorland colouring. The purple undertones set it apart from a conventional red multi, and suit both period matching, where purple bricks are common, and contemporary schemes.

name: Chepstow Multi
description: Chepstow Multi blends warm reds and browns with darker mottling across each face, lending walls depth with a soft border-country warmth. It is an unshowy, dependable multi that works as readily across a whole elevation as on a single extension, and takes grey or buff mortar comfortably.

name: Traditional Red Blend Brick Slip
description: Traditional Red Blend in slip form offers warm reds and browns with a lightly weathered face, in a thin format for internal walls, chimney breasts and cladding systems. It gives interiors the familiar warmth of traditional English brickwork without the depth of a full brick skin. Well suited to feature walls, chimney breasts, retail fit-outs and retrofit insulation systems.

name: Weathered Gault Blend
description: Weathered Gault Blend draws on gault clay, which fires to the pale creams and soft yellows found in brickwork across Cambridgeshire and the eastern counties. The weathered treatment adds darker patches and irregularity, so a new wall reads as established rather than newly built. It suits period extensions, infill and garden walls in gault brick areas.

name: Kinder Mixed Red
description: Kinder Mixed Red brings together warm reds with browns and occasional darker bricks, giving elevations depth and a robust Peak District character. The mix is broad enough to add real interest and consistent enough to specify confidently across a whole house or a larger development.

name: Hampstead Yellow
description: Hampstead Yellow is a soft London yellow with gentle variation and a gently worked surface, carrying the traditional brightness of the capital's yellow brickwork without pretending to be a weathered stock. A straightforward choice for extensions, infill and garden walls in yellow brick areas of London and beyond. The lightly varied colouring keeps larger elevations from reading as flat.

name: Sheerwater Silver Yellow
description: Sheerwater Silver Yellow is an unusual pairing, combining soft yellow tones with a cooler silvery-grey cast across the same face. The result is brighter than a grey and calmer than a yellow, which gives contemporary elevations a distinctive quality that neither colour achieves alone.

name: Renaissance
description: Renaissance is a warm, richly toned brick with layered colouring that shifts across each face, giving elevations depth and a slightly classical warmth. It is a brick with presence rather than neutrality, working well on feature elevations and houses where the brickwork is intended to be noticed.

name: Leamington Buff Multi
description: Leamington Buff Multi blends pale sandy buffs with warmer cream and light brown tones, giving elevations brightness while keeping enough variation to avoid looking flat. Buff brickwork sits comfortably with render, stone and timber, making it useful on contemporary and traditional schemes alike.

name: Welbourne Antique Brick Slip
description: Welbourne Antique as a brick slip carries darkened, weathered colouring across a worn and irregular face, giving interior brickwork the appearance of a wall that has stood for generations. Well suited to feature walls, period conversions and fit-outs where an aged finish is wanted at limited depth. Corner slips are needed at external angles, so allow for these when calculating quantities.

name: Draycott Red Multi
description: Warm reds with browns and darker mottling worked across each face, giving depth that holds up over large areas of walling. An unfussy, reliable multi that neither demands special treatment nor limits what you put next to it. Sensible for a full development, a rear extension or a boundary wall without needing to think too hard about it.

name: Clent Russet Mixture
description: Russet reds warmed with browns and softer orange, drawn from the colouring of the Worcestershire hills it takes its name from. The mixture reads rich without going dark, and lifts noticeably in low morning and evening light. Rural extensions and village infill are its natural home, though it holds up perfectly well on a suburban semi.

name: Woodland Mixture
description: A broad mix of browns, russets and softer greens-in-shadow tones that recalls timber and bark more than conventional brickwork. The spread between individual bricks is wide, so walls build up with the uneven, organic quality of something that grew rather than something specified. Suits rural extensions, garden structures and houses sitting among trees.

name: Tuscan Red Multi
description: Warm terracotta reds with softer earth tones blended through, borrowing the palette of Italian farmhouses and rooftops. It reads sunlit rather than fiery, which makes it easier to live with over a full elevation than a stronger red multi. Reliable across whole houses, garden walls and extensions, and forgiving about what you point it with.

name: Sunset Red Multi
description: Reds warmed with orange and amber across each face, catching light the way the name suggests. It brings genuine energy to an elevation, particularly one facing west, and works well as a warmer counterpoint banded against grey or buff brickwork. On a north-facing wall it loses much of what makes it interesting, so think about orientation before committing.

name: Cedarwood Multi
description: Warm browns shot through with red and softer tan tones, named for the timber it echoes. Brown sits in useful territory between the neutrality of grey and the commitment of red, and this one keeps enough variation across each face to stop a long elevation flattening out. Works particularly hard alongside timber cladding and stone.

name: Caldera Red Multi
description: Deep, fiery reds with darker scorched tones running through, named for the volcanic crater it evokes. There is more drama here than in an everyday red multi, which makes it a choice for elevations meant to be looked at rather than looked past. Pair it with a dark mortar and the whole wall goes furnace-like; a paler joint pulls it back considerably.

name: Shipley Blend
description: Warm reds and browns softened with neutral tones over a gently worked face. The blend is restrained rather than dramatic, which makes it easy to pair with whatever else is going on across the elevation, from render to timber to stone. Bricks like this tend to be specified when the brickwork is deliberately not the story, and the windows or the roofline are.

name: Arley Red Rustic
description: A warm red body finished with a roughened, textured face that throws shadow across an elevation and stops the colour reading as flat. Traditional and rural settings suit it best, though it sits perfectly happily on a suburban extension. Made in both the metric height and a 73mm imperial for older coursing.

name: Berkshire Red
description: A mellow Home Counties red with soft variation and a faintly grained face, carrying the gentler colouring of southern brickwork rather than a hard industrial red. Comfortable alongside period properties, which makes it a common pick for extensions and garden walls. A soft lime-toned mortar and a struck joint will get you closer to a period match than the brick choice alone ever does.

name: Kemsley Yellow
description: A soft warm yellow with gentle variation, carrying the traditional brightness of English yellow brickwork without pretending to be a weathered stock. Straightforward stuff for extensions and infill in yellow brick areas, where a red would look plainly wrong. It sits comfortably beside genuine stock brick without trying to imitate it, which is often exactly what an extension needs.

name: Titian
description: Named for the painter and his particular red, this is a rich warm brick with real depth of colour and subtle movement across the face. It gives an elevation presence without going dark, and holds its warmth even in flat overcast light. Best given room to work, on a feature elevation or a whole facade, rather than fighting for attention beside other strong materials.

name: Bourneville Buff Blend
description: Pale sandy buffs blended with cream and light brown, bright enough to lift an elevation without the flatness of a single uniform colour. Buff sits easily with render, stone and timber, so it turns up on contemporary schemes as often as traditional ones. Order a sample and look at it in overcast light as well as sun, since pale bricks shift character more than dark ones between the two.

name: Autumn Russet Sovereign Stock
description: Russet and amber tones over the creased, softened face of a stock brick, giving both the colour of autumn and the irregularity of traditional stock production. The two together produce a wall that looks like it has been standing a while, which is exactly what period extensions and garden walls tend to need.

name: Oatmeal Blend
description: Soft neutral tones through pale oatmeal and light buff, blended so the wall keeps quiet depth without pattern. It is a restrained, undemanding brick that sits comfortably beside render, timber, stone and glazing on contemporary and traditional work alike. A good candidate where the brickwork needs to recede and let another material take the lead.

name: Docklands Yellow Multi
description: Warm yellows blended with buff and darker brown tones, echoing the stock brickwork of London's riverside warehouses. Bright enough to lift a wall, varied enough to look like it has been there a while. A natural fit for conversions, urban infill and extensions in yellow brick streets.

name: Windmill Orange Multi
description: Orange runs right through this one, warmed further by browns and the odd darker brick scattered across the blend. It has the sunlit, slightly rustic quality of older farm and mill buildings, and comes into its own on west-facing walls that catch the last of the afternoon. Popular for extensions, garden walls and infill in orange brick districts.

name: Nevada Buff
description: A pale, sun-bleached buff with soft movement across the face, warm enough to avoid feeling clinical but decidedly bright. It suits contemporary work particularly well and pairs cleanly with dark window frames, glazing and light timber. Splashback at ground level is the thing to detail out, since it shows on a pale brick far sooner than on a dark one.

name: Reclaimed Shire Sovereign Stock
description: Built to look salvaged from a country wall that came down decades ago: worn reds and browns, darker weathered bricks scattered through, and the creased irregular face of traditional stock production. All the character of genuine reclaims, with sizes that actually match and stock you can rely on turning up.

name: Sienna Red
description: Named after the earth pigment, and it earns it: a warm burnt-orange red with real saturation and depth. The colour holds up strongly in flat light, which is more than many reds manage, and gives an elevation genuine presence without going dark. One to keep away from other strong colours, though, since it does not share an elevation quietly.

name: Tabasco Red Multi
description: A hot, saturated red with darker tones running through it, and the name is not modest about it. This is a brick for elevations meant to carry colour, holding its intensity in flat overcast light where softer reds tend to go grey. Used sparingly, as a feature panel or banding, it earns its keep more easily than across four full elevations.

name: Ewhurst Medium Multi
description: Sitting at medium depth between the lighter and darker options, this blend of reds and browns is one of the easier bricks to match into an existing wall. That middle register is precisely why it turns up so often on extensions and repair work, where the job is to blend rather than announce.

name: Dunsfold Multi
description: A Surrey-flavoured blend of reds and browns with darker mottling worked across each face. Nothing about it shouts, which is the point: it gives an elevation depth and then gets out of the way of the windows, doors and detailing. A safe specification across whole houses as readily as single extensions.

name: Pembridge Red
description: A warm border-country red with soft variation and a lightly worked face, mellow rather than hard-edged. It settles beside older brickwork without fuss, which is why it appears so often on extensions to period cottages and farmhouses. Check the coursing on the original wall before you order, as farmhouse brickwork is rarely built to modern gauge.

name: Kingsley Multi
description: Reds and browns blended with lighter and darker bricks throughout, giving a wall genuine movement without ever tipping into busy. It is an everyday multi in the best sense, dependable enough for a full development and characterful enough for a single rear extension. Worth ordering a sample if you are matching against something existing, since the mid-range tones can read warmer or cooler depending on what sits beside them.

name: Lingfield Red Multi
description: Warm reds worked through with browns and the occasional darker brick, giving a wall real movement without heavy contrast. A dependable Surrey and Sussex multi, broad enough to hold interest across a full development and forgiving about mortar choice. Fine across a whole house, a rear extension or a long run of boundary wall without needing much thought.

name: Chartham Multi
description: A Kentish blend of reds and browns softened with neutral tones, carrying the gentle variation of established brickwork rather than the strong contrast of a heavy multi. Easy to pair with existing materials, which is why it turns up so often on extensions rather than new builds.

name: Harvest Buff Multi
description: Sandy buffs warmed with cream and light brown, named for the field colours it borrows. Bright enough to open up an elevation, varied enough to avoid the flatness that catches out plain pale bricks. Comfortable beside render, stone and timber. A dark mortar against it makes a strong graphic wall, which suits contemporary work particularly well.

name: Warm Golden Buff
description: Buff with the warmth turned up, sitting in honey and gold territory rather than plain sand. The colour lifts strongly in low sun and stays pleasant in flat light, which is not something every pale brick manages. Comfortable beside stone, render and timber on both traditional and contemporary work.

name: Tawny Buff
description: Sandy buff pushed towards the warmer, tawnier end of the range, with soft movement across the face. It brings brightness to an elevation without the chill of a grey or the flatness of a plain white, and pairs easily with timber, stone and off-white render. Straightforward to build with and forgiving about what you point it with.

name: Trinity Cream Gilt
description: Soft cream lifted by the golden highlights the Gilt range is built around. The effect is delicate rather than showy, giving a pale wall subtle warmth and depth in raking light where a flat cream would simply look flat. Suits contemporary schemes and areas where stone or render sets the tone rather than red brick.

name: Gilt Yellow Multi
description: Golden yellows blended with buff and softer brown, the gilt highlights lifting the whole across each face. There is enough variation here to look established rather than new, which suits extensions and garden walls in yellow brick districts. Mix from several packs as you lay so the darker bricks spread evenly rather than gathering in one bay.

name: Durham Claret
description: A deep wine red with plum undertones, considerably more formal in character than an everyday facing red. The darker body holds its presence over large areas, which suits apartment schemes, urban housing and anywhere the palette is meant to feel considered. It also does good work as a darker banding course set against a lighter brick.

name: Gilt Smoked Orange Multi
description: The orange of the Gilt family with smoked, darkened patches laid over it, adding age and weight. The smoking varies from brick to brick, so the wall gains the uneven darkening of brickwork that has stood in a town for a few decades. Useful where new brickwork has to sit beside something genuinely old without looking freshly delivered.

name: Durham Red Multi
description: Warm reds blended with browns and the occasional darker brick, giving depth across a wall without heavy contrast. A dependable northern multi, broad enough to hold interest and consistent enough to specify across a whole development with confidence. Straightforward to lay, forgiving on mortar choice, and consistent enough to order in quantity.

name: Gilt Red Multi
description: Warm reds lifted with golden highlights and softer brown tones, giving more life than a conventional red multi manages. The gilt quality shows most in raking light, when the highlights catch and the wall gains a subtle glow. Sensible for housing and extensions where a plain red would feel flat but a strong multi would be too much.

name: London Stock
description: The brick that built the capital. Soft yellow-to-buff bodies, smoky creased faces, and tone shifting from one brick to the next so a finished wall reads weathered rather than flat. Made in both the standard metric height and a 68mm imperial for the Georgian and Victorian coursing it is usually asked to match.

name: Capelwick Multi
description: Reds and browns with darker mottling worked across each face, giving a wall depth that holds up over a long run of brickwork. It is an unshowy blend, the sort specified when the elevation needs interest but not a focal point. Fine across a whole house or a single rear extension.

name: Ashington Red Multi
description: Warm reds worked through with browns and darker mottling, carrying the solid, unpretentious character of northern brickwork. It does the job across a full elevation without asking for attention, and takes grey or buff mortar equally well. A practical choice for housing, extensions and boundary walls where reliability matters more than making a statement.

name: Gilt Yellow
description: A warm golden yellow with the gilt highlights the range is built around, cleaner and more consistent than the multi version. Bright, warm and even, it suits extensions and infill in yellow brick areas where a strongly varied brick would be too much. Pair it with an off-white mortar and the warmth carries; grey will cool it more than you might expect.

name: Maplehurst Light Multi
description: The lighter end of the multi range, mixing soft reds and buffs with paler bricks throughout. It brightens an elevation while keeping the varied quality of a traditional wall, which is a useful combination on extensions to lighter period brickwork. Worth seeing a laid panel rather than judging from a single brick, since light multis change character noticeably at scale.

name: Waresley Orange
description: Warm terracotta orange with gentle variation, sunnier than a conventional red without tipping into anything garish. It comes alive on west-facing walls in the late afternoon, and holds its warmth better than most oranges in overcast conditions. Good for extensions, garden walls and infill where the surrounding brickwork already leans orange.

name: Cinnabar Red Multi
description: Named for the vivid mineral pigment, and the colouring lives up to it: strong warm reds with orange running through and darker tones for depth. It carries an elevation on colour alone, and stands up well in flat light where softer reds fade back. Think about how much of it you want before committing to four elevations of it.

name: Gilt Orange Multi
description: Warm orange tones with gilt highlights and softer browns worked through, part of a family built around that golden quality. The orange lifts strongly in low sun, making it a good candidate for west-facing elevations and warmer contrast banding. Buff mortar keeps the gold forward; grey mutes it and leaves you with a fairly ordinary orange.

name: Mulberry Red
description: A deep berry red with purple undertones, richer and cooler than a conventional facing red. The colour gives an elevation weight and a slightly formal air, which suits urban housing and apartment schemes better than a bright red would. It holds up across a full elevation without going gloomy, which not every dark red manages.

name: Sandalwood Yellow Multi
description: Warm sandy yellows blended with light brown and softer neutral tones, part of the same family as the plain Sandalwood but with noticeably more going on across each face. The extra variation suits larger elevations where a single flat tone risks looking dull. Worth seeing both laid side by side before choosing, as the difference is more obvious in a wall than in the hand.

name: Waresley Red
description: A clean warm red with a faintly worked face and modest variation, even across a large elevation without going lifeless. There is nothing complicated about it, which is much of the appeal: it does the job on housing, extensions and boundary walls and lets the detailing round it do the talking.

name: Gilt Smoked Yellow Multi
description: Golden yellows overlaid with smoky darkened patches, combining brightness with the aged quality of weathered stock brickwork. It occupies useful ground between a clean yellow and a full weathered stock, bright enough to lift a wall while still looking settled. A soft lime-toned mortar reinforces the aged quality; a crisp grey works against it.

name: Witton Multi
description: Reds and browns mixed with softer neutral tones, producing a wall with balanced movement that works at any scale. An easy blend to build with, adding depth to an elevation without dictating what happens around it. Fine across a whole house, and equally at home on a single extension or a run of garden wall.

name: Nottingham Red Rustic
description: A warm red with a roughened, textured face that gives an elevation shadow and depth. The rustic finish reads traditional and hard-wearing without tipping into antique, making it a practical choice for housing, extensions and garden walls in the Midlands and beyond. Keep the face clean as you lay rather than planning to clean down afterwards, which is always more work.

name: Rudgwick Multi
description: Reds and browns with darker mottling across each face, giving an elevation warmth and depth without heavy contrast. A quiet, reliable Sussex multi that works as readily on a full house as on a run of garden wall, and takes grey or buff mortar equally well.

name: Clumber Red
description: A clean warm red with modest variation and a faintly grained face, even across a large elevation without going lifeless. Straightforward and dependable, suited to housing, extensions and boundary walls where the brick is meant to be a background rather than a feature. Undemanding about mortar and easy to lay, which counts for something on a large job.

name: Old English Mixture Rustic
description: Traditional reds and browns blended broadly, then finished with a roughened rustic face. Colour variation and surface texture working together give a wall genuine depth, which suits period extensions, cottages and rural projects where uniformity would be a drawback. Traditional bonds such as Flemish reinforce the period look, though stretcher bond is perfectly acceptable on modern cavity work.

name: Warnham Red
description: A mellow Sussex red with soft variation and a gently worked face, warm rather than hard-edged. It settles beside period brickwork without fuss, which is why it appears so regularly on extensions to older houses in the south east. Check the coursing on the original wall before ordering, since a good colour match counts for little if the courses drift.

name: Kirton Arden Red
description: A warm mid red with gentle variation and a lightly worked face, unfussy and easy to build with. It gives an elevation warmth and consistency in equal measure, which makes it a safe specification across housing and extensions alike. Good background brick, in the sense that the windows and detailing get to do the talking.

name: Southdown Multi
description: Reds and browns blended with softer tones, named for the Sussex downland it comes from. The variation is gentle and the overall effect settled, which suits extensions and garden walls in areas where the existing brickwork has long since mellowed. A sensible default where the brickwork needs to support the building rather than define it.

name: Olde Autumn Antique
description: Autumnal reds and browns under a deliberately aged, darkened face, so a new wall looks like it has been standing a good while by the time you point it. Best suited to period extensions, barn conversions and anywhere a fresh brick would look plainly out of place beside the original.

name: Kimbolton Red Multi
description: Warm reds worked through with browns and darker mottling, giving depth across a wall without heavy contrast. A reliable everyday multi, forgiving about mortar choice and consistent enough to order in quantity for a full development. A safe specification for housing, extensions and boundary walls where dependability matters more than character.

name: Olde Horsham
description: Warm reds and browns over a worn, softly irregular face, drawn from the brickwork of the Sussex town it takes its name from. It has the settled, slightly weathered quality of a wall that has been standing since long before anyone thought about cavity construction.

name: Winchester Multi
description: Warm reds and browns blended with softer neutral tones, carrying the composed quality associated with Hampshire brickwork. Variation is present but restrained, which makes it easy to specify across a whole house without the wall becoming the loudest thing on the site. Equally comfortable on a new build, an extension or a run of garden wall.

name: Olde Henfield Multi
description: A Sussex blend running through warm reds and browns with a lightly weathered, irregular face. The colouring is gentle rather than strong, which lets new brickwork settle beside an older wall instead of drawing the eye to the join. Suits extensions, garden walls and infill across the Weald, where the local stock has long since mellowed.

name: Olde Cranleigh Multi
description: Reds and browns blended over a softly irregular face, carrying the unforced variation of Surrey village brickwork. It builds up with genuine tonal movement, which suits cottage extensions and rural infill far better than anything uniform would. A soft lime mortar and a struck joint will get you closer to the period look than the brick alone.

name: Chatsworth Grey Rustic
description: Soft grey with a roughened, textured face, which is an unusual pairing and a useful one. The texture stops grey brickwork reading as the flat modern plane it often becomes, giving an elevation depth while keeping the contemporary colour. Useful where a contemporary colour has to sit alongside older buildings without looking newly dropped in.

name: Warnham Terracotta
description: The Warnham body pushed into terracotta territory, warm and orange-leaning with soft variation across the face. It has the sunlit quality of old clay tile and lifts strongly in low light, making it a good pick for elevations that catch the morning or evening. On a north-facing elevation you lose most of that, so orientation is worth thinking about before you commit.

name: Lindum Cottage Red Multi
description: Reds and browns blended over a softly irregular face, aimed at the cottage and village work its name suggests. The variation is broad enough to feel traditional, and the worn face keeps new brickwork from looking freshly delivered beside something older. Compare a sample against the existing wall in daylight, and check the coursing while you have the tape out.

name: Farmstead Antique
description: Worn reds and browns under darkened, patchy weathering, with the irregular face of brickwork that has weathered on an exposed farm building for a century. It suits barn conversions, agricultural extensions and rural work where anything crisp would look wrong. A soft lime-toned mortar reinforces the weathered quality considerably; crisp grey pointing works against it.

name: Clumber Red Mixture
description: The Clumber red opened out into a broader mixture, with browns and lighter and darker bricks running through. The extra spread gives a wall considerably more depth, which suits larger elevations where a single flat colour risks looking dull. Draw from three or four packs at once and keep mixing, or the tonal spread will band.

name: Olde Sussex Blend
description: A broad mix of reds, browns and softer weathered tones over irregular faces, echoing the unplanned brickwork of Sussex farms and cottages. The spread between bricks is wide, so walls come out looking accumulated rather than specified. Cottage extensions, village infill and garden structures are where it earns its keep.

name: Ashwell Yellow Multi
description: Warm yellows blended with buff and softer brown tones, bright enough to lift a wall and varied enough to look established rather than newly delivered. A sensible option for extensions and infill in yellow brick districts, where a red would look plainly imported. An off-white or soft buff mortar keeps it warm; grey will cool the yellow more than you might expect.

name: Yorkshire Red Blend
description: Warm reds and browns blended with the solid, hard-working character of northern brickwork. Nothing decorative about it, which is rather the point: it gives an elevation warmth and depth and then gets on with being a wall. Forgiving on mortar choice, straightforward to lay, and consistent enough to order in quantity.

name: Sherwood Red Mixture
description: Warm reds blended with browns and the odd darker brick, giving an elevation depth and a solid Midlands character. Broad enough to hold interest across a large area, consistent enough to specify with confidence on a whole development. Forgiving about mortar and straightforward to lay in quantity.

name: Nutcombe Multi
description: Warm browns and reds blended with softer neutral tones, sitting in that useful middle ground between the neutrality of grey and the commitment of a full red. It pairs particularly well with timber and stone, and gives a long elevation depth without shouting about it.

name: Burghley Red Rustic
description: A warm red finished with a roughened, textured face that throws shadow across an elevation and keeps the colour from reading flat. Traditional in feel without going as far as an antique brick, which makes it a practical middle ground for housing and extensions. Good across whole elevations, garden walls and anywhere a plain smooth red would feel too clean.

name: Olde Heritage Antique
description: Darkened, patchy weathering over worn reds and browns, with an irregular face that reads as genuinely old rather than merely rustic. It is aimed squarely at restoration and period extension work, where the brief is to disappear into what is already there. Expect it to look slightly fresher than the wall beside it for the first year or two; that gap closes on its own.

name: LBC Regency
description: Composed colouring with restrained variation, aimed at the elegance of Regency brickwork rather than the rougher character of a village wall. It suits urban extensions, apartment schemes and elevations where a considered finish matters more than rustic charm. Check the coursing on the original wall before ordering, since a good colour match counts for little if the courses drift.

name: LBC Cotswold
description: Soft honey and buff tones borrowed from Cotswold stone, aimed at areas where the vernacular is pale rather than red. It gives new brickwork a mellow warmth that sits far more comfortably beside stone than any red would manage. Compare it against the actual stone you are building next to, since honey tones vary considerably from quarry to quarry.

name: LBC Honey Buff
description: Warm honey tones over a buff base, brighter and sweeter than a plain sandy brick. The colour glows in low sun and stays warm in overcast conditions, making it a reliable pale option where a neutral buff would feel too cool. A reliable choice for housing, extensions and garden walls where the elevation needs lifting.

name: Village Oatmeal Buff Multi
description: Pale oatmeal and sandy buff tones blended with light brown, bright without being stark and varied enough to avoid the flatness that catches out plain pale bricks. It sits comfortably beside render, stone and timber on traditional and contemporary work alike. Splashback at ground level is the detail to get right, since it shows on a pale brick far sooner than a dark one.

name: LBC Golden Buff
description: Buff pushed towards gold, warm and bright with gentle variation across the face. It lifts an elevation without the chill of a pale neutral, and holds its warmth in flat light better than most bricks at this end of the range. Pairs cleanly with timber, stone and off-white render on contemporary and traditional work alike.

name: LBC Georgian
description: Restrained colouring and a composed face aimed at the proportion and formality of Georgian brickwork. It avoids the heavy mottling of a rustic multi in favour of something more even, which is closer to how better quality eighteenth century walls actually read. Mortar colour and joint profile do as much work as the brick on period matching, so plan both together.

name: LBC Common Flettons
description: The plain workhorse of British building for the best part of a century. Fletton production from Peterborough clay gave the trade an economical brick for internal walls, rendered elevations and anything that would never be seen. The face is simple and the colour sits in the pinkish red range with mild variation.

name: LBC Heather
description: Purples and browns softening a red base, which is what heather colouring means in practice. It has been laid on countless British houses and remains a safe, attractive choice for housing, extensions and garden walls. Made in the standard metric height and a 73mm imperial for older coursing.

name: LBC Longville Stone
description: Pale stone-toned colouring with soft variation, aimed at areas where the vernacular runs to stone rather than brick. It gives new work a muted, quiet quality that sits comfortably beside genuine stone without pretending to be it. Local planning in stone areas can be particular, so check before ordering and expect to provide a sample panel.

name: LBC Milton Buff
