description: A soft sandy buff with gentle movement across the face, straightforward and undemanding. It brightens an elevation without drama and pairs cleanly with most materials, which is why it appears so regularly on housing and extensions across the country. Undemanding about mortar and easy to lay in quantity, which counts on a large job.

name: LBC Sandfaced
description: Sand applied to the face during manufacture leaves a fine grainy texture and a softer, matt appearance. That surface scatters light rather than reflecting it, which is much closer to how older brickwork reads and helps new work settle beside an existing wall. Keep the face clean as you lay, since a grainy surface holds mortar splashes more readily than a smooth one.

name: LBC Rustic
description: A warm red body with the textured, patterned face the Rustic name has meant for decades. The surface catches light and shadow across an elevation, giving a rougher and more traditional look than any smooth brick manages. Made in the standard metric height and a 73mm imperial.

name: LBC Nene Valley
description: Warm reds and browns blended with softer tones, named for the river valley where the LBC works have long stood. The variation is gentle and the overall effect settled, which makes it easy to specify across a whole house without the wall dominating. Forgiving about mortar choice and straightforward to lay, on a garden wall or a full development.

name: LBC Hereward Light
description: A pale, softly varied brick at the lighter end of the LBC range, bright enough to open up an elevation while keeping enough movement to avoid looking flat. Easy to pair with render, timber and stone on both contemporary and traditional schemes. Splashback at ground level is the detail to get right, since it shows on a pale brick far sooner than a dark one.

name: LBC Regrades
description: Regrades are bricks that fall outside the standard grading for appearance, sold accordingly. Colour and face vary more widely than a graded brick, which makes them a practical option for garden walls, outbuildings, rendered work and anywhere the finish is not critical. Order a sample first so you can judge how much variation you are actually taking on.

name: LBC Dapple Light
description: Dappled light and dark tones scattered across a pale base, giving a wall movement without the weight of a full multi. The effect is subtle at distance and more obvious close up, which suits elevations that need interest without becoming busy. Worth seeing a laid panel rather than a single brick, as the dappling reads very differently at scale.

name: LBC Ironstone
description: Deep rusty reds and browns with the darker, mineral quality the name suggests. It reads heavier and more weathered than a standard red, giving an elevation real presence, and works particularly well in areas where ironstone appears in the local building stock. Best given room to work across a full elevation rather than fighting for attention beside other strong materials.

name: LBC Rustic Antique
description: The familiar textured Rustic face with darker, aged tones laid over it, so brickwork looks settled rather than newly built. It suits period extensions, conservation areas and garden walls where a fresh red would jar against what is already there. Available in metric and 73mm imperial heights.

name: LBC Brecken Grey
description: A soft grey from the London Brick Company range, with gentle tonal movement that keeps a large elevation from reading as one flat plane. Grey brickwork has become a mainstay of contemporary housing, and this is a dependable, widely available way into it. Pairs cleanly with dark window frames, glazing and timber cladding, which is most of why it gets specified.

name: LBC Chiltern
description: Soft browns and buffs blended with warmer tones, taking its name from the hills whose colouring it borrows. It sits in gentle, unassuming territory that pairs easily with flint, stone and render, which is much of why it turns up across the Home Counties on extensions and village work.

name: LBC Brindle
description: Streaked, mottled colouring is what brindling means, and here darker tones run across a warm red-brown base. The effect gives a wall genuine surface interest and a traditional, hard-wearing look without the weight of a full antique brick. Suits period extensions and elevations wanting character without the commitment of a heavily weathered brick.

name: LBC Claydon Red Multi
description: Warm reds worked through with browns and darker mottling, giving an elevation depth without heavy contrast. A dependable multi from a range that has been laid on more British housing than almost any other, and forgiving about mortar choice. Sensible for housing, extensions and boundary walls where reliability matters more than making a statement.

name: Village Sunglow
description: Warm golden and orange tones with soft variation, named for the light it seems to hold. It brings genuine glow to an elevation in low sun and stays pleasant in flat conditions, which is more than many warm bricks manage. Good for extensions, garden walls and rural infill.

name: LBC Saxon Gold
description: Golden buff tones with warm highlights, bright and mellow at the same time. It gives a pale elevation genuine warmth, avoiding the coolness that catches out plain neutral buffs, and pairs particularly well with timber and stone. Good for housing, extensions and garden walls where a neutral pale brick would feel too cold.

name: Village Russet Red Mixture
description: Russet reds warmed with browns and softer orange, blended broadly enough to feel like traditional village brickwork rather than modern production. The colouring reads rich without going dark, and lifts noticeably in low morning and evening light. Buff mortar keeps the warmth forward; grey pulls it towards something more ordinary.

name: Staff Slate Blue Smooth Perf (Facing Quality)
description: Staffordshire blue in a slate-toned variant, smooth faced, perforated and selected to facing quality. The slate cast reads slightly greyer and less inky than a standard blue, which some prefer where the brickwork is on show rather than buried below ground. Commonly used for plinths, string courses and contrast banding as well as general engineering work.

name: Windermere Blue (Facing Quality)
description: Blue engineering brick selected to facing quality, so it can be used where the brickwork is on show rather than buried below ground. The dense body and dark blue-grey face give plinths, string courses and contrast banding the sharp definition that blue brickwork is valued for.

name: KR20 White
description: A clean white finish, the palest option in the KR range. White reads sharp and contemporary, throwing joints and detailing into strong relief, and works particularly well where the aim is a crisp, graphic wall rather than a warm or weathered one. Please speak to us about suitable applications and any limitations before ordering.

name: Medway Blend
description: Warm reds and browns with softer tones blended through, drawing on the brickmaking tradition of the Medway valley. The variation is moderate and the character settled, making it a comfortable choice for Kent extensions and infill work. Equally at home on a new build, an extension or a run of garden wall.

name: K209 Class B Perf Blue
description: A perforated Class B engineering brick in Staffordshire blue, the standard choice for damp proof courses, plinths, retaining walls, manholes and general engineering work. Dense, dark and hard-wearing, with the low water absorption the classification demands. The 65mm metric height suits new build coursing; ask us about imperial availability for matching work.

name: Brunel Blue Smooth Perf (Facing Quality)
description: Staffordshire blue with a smooth face, perforated, and selected to facing quality so it can be used where the brickwork will be seen. The dense body and dark blue-grey sheen suit plinths, string courses and contrast banding as readily as the below-ground work blues are traditionally specified for.

name: LBC Windsor
description: Warm reds and browns blended with a composed, slightly formal quality. Variation is present but controlled, which makes it a comfortable specification across whole elevations where a strong multi would become tiring to look at. Forgiving on mortar and consistent enough to order in quantity for a full development.

name: Atherstone Red
description: A clean warm red with modest variation and a lightly worked face, even across a large elevation without going lifeless. Unfussy and dependable, suited to housing, extensions and boundary walls where the brickwork is meant to be a background. Undemanding about mortar and easy to lay, which counts for something across a large elevation.

name: Oakthorpe Red
description: A warm mid red with gentle variation and a faintly grained face, straightforward and easy to build with. It gives an elevation warmth and consistency in equal measure, which makes it a safe specification across housing and extensions alike. A good background brick, in the sense that the windows and detailing get to do the talking.

name: Hampton Rural Blend
description: Reds, browns and softer tones blended broadly over a lightly worn face, aimed at the unplanned look of country brickwork. It builds up with genuine variation, which suits rural extensions, farm buildings and village infill better than anything uniform. A soft lime mortar and a struck joint get you closer to the period look than the brick choice alone.

name: LBC Tudor
description: Deep red-brown with dark mottling and a lightly rustic face, one of the most widely laid bricks in the country. It gives a wall real depth and an aged, traditional feel straight off the pallet, at a price that has kept it on housing schemes for decades. Metric and 73mm imperial heights available.

name: Chelsea Smoked Red
description: A warm red overlaid with smoky darker patches, imitating the way London brickwork darkened through decades of coal smoke. The effect adds depth and age without going as far as a full antique, which suits urban extensions and infill particularly well. A soft lime-toned mortar reinforces the aged quality, where a crisp grey works against it.

name: Oakthorpe Red Multi
description: The Oakthorpe red with browns and darker mottling worked across each face, giving depth across a wall without heavy contrast. A dependable everyday multi, forgiving about mortar and consistent enough to order in quantity for a full development. Fine across a whole house or a single rear extension without needing much thought.

name: K109 Class B Solid Blue
description: A solid Class B engineering brick in Staffordshire blue, without perforations. Solid blues are what you need for copings, cappings, cills and other details where holes would show or hold water, as well as general engineering work below damp proof course. Please confirm the current declared performance figures with us before finalising any specification.

name: Red Class B Solid
description: A solid Class B engineering brick in even red, without perforations. Solid bricks are what you need for copings, cappings, cills and anywhere the brick will be cut or exposed on edge, since there are no holes to show or to hold water. Commonly specified alongside the perforated version, which handles the general walling while the solids take the details.

name: Autumn Glow Multi
description: The same golden amber warmth with far more variation across each face, browns and darker bricks blended through. The extra depth suits larger elevations, where the plain version can start to look uniform over a long run of walling. On a north-facing wall much of the warmth is lost, so orientation is worth a thought before committing.

name: Greyfriars Gault
description: Pale gault colouring in soft creams and greys, quiet and composed rather than warm. Gault brickwork has a distinctly eastern and London character, and this one gives contemporary work a muted pale option that sits well against glazing and dark frames. Useful on contemporary schemes wanting a pale brick without the warmth of a buff.

name: K201 Staffordshire Smooth Blue (Facing Quality)
description: The classic Staffordshire smooth blue, selected to facing quality. Near-vitrified, dense and dark, with the clean smooth face that has made blue brickwork a staple of Victorian engineering and a striking contrast against red or buff ever since. Worth trialling a panel before committing, since mortar colour changes blue brickwork dramatically.

name: Belgravia Gault Blend
description: Gault clay fires pale rather than red, which is where the creams and soft yellows of eastern England come from. Blended here with subtle variation, it gives an elevation the composed, slightly formal quality associated with better London and Home Counties brickwork. A pale mortar keeps it quiet and unified; a darker joint picks out the bond pattern sharply.

name: Ardleigh Yellow Stock
description: Soft yellows and buffs over the creased, irregular face of traditional stock production, with darker bricks scattered through. The colouring and the surface together give a wall the weathered quality of established Essex and East Anglian brickwork. A natural fit for period extensions, garden walls and infill in yellow stock districts.

name: Autumn Glow
description: Warm golden and amber tones with soft variation, holding light the way the name suggests. It brings genuine glow to an elevation in low sun and stays pleasant in flat conditions, which is more than many warm bricks manage. Good for extensions, garden walls and rural infill where a cooler brick would feel wrong.

name: LBC Sunset Red Multi
description: Reds warmed with orange and amber across each face, catching low light the way the name promises. It brings energy to an elevation, particularly a west-facing one, and works well banded as a warmer counterpoint against grey or buff brickwork. Buff or cream mortar preserves the warmth; grey cools it and mutes the orange considerably.

name: Red Class B Perf
description: A perforated Class B engineering brick in solid, even red. The dense body brings the strength and low water absorption the classification is known for, while the clean red face keeps it presentable where the brickwork will be seen. Made in both the standard metric height and a 73mm imperial for matching older coursing.

name: KR22 Oak Buff
description: A warm oak-toned buff, sitting between sand and light brown with the mellow quality the name suggests. It is the most naturally warm option in the KR range, pairing easily with timber, stone and off-white render without the coolness of the greys. Please speak to us about suitable applications and any limitations before ordering.

name: Atherstone Red Multi
description: The Atherstone red opened out, with browns and lighter and darker bricks running through the blend. The extra spread gives a wall considerably more depth, which suits larger elevations where a single flat colour risks looking dull. Draw from three or four packs at once and keep mixing, or the tonal spread will band.

name: Ember Blend
description: Deep glowing reds with darker scorched tones running through, named for the coals it recalls. There is more heat in this than an everyday red multi, which makes it a choice for elevations meant to be looked at rather than looked past. Pair it with a dark mortar and the whole wall goes furnace-like; a paler joint pulls it back considerably.

name: Lanzarote Black
description: Deep volcanic black with just enough surface movement to keep a large area from reading as one flat plane. Black brickwork has become a signature of contemporary architecture, and this one delivers it without the coating that some dark finishes rely on. Dark surfaces absorb more heat than pale ones, which is worth remembering for planting set tight against the wall.

name: Chatterley Red
description: A warm Staffordshire red with gentle variation and a lightly worked face, drawing on a clay tradition better known for its blues. It gives an elevation warmth and consistency in equal measure, unfussy and straightforward to build with at any scale. A good background brick, in the sense that the windows and detailing get to do the talking.

name: KR42 Lavendar Brown
description: An unusual pairing of brown with a lavender cast, cooler and more muted than a straightforward brown. The purple undertone gives it a quality neither a plain brown nor a grey quite achieves, useful where something less predictable is wanted. Worth seeing in person, since the undertone is difficult to judge from a photograph.

name: KR74 Light Grey
description: A soft light grey, the paler of the two greys in the KR range. It gives a calm, neutral finish that sits comfortably with dark frames, glazing and timber, and keeps a large area from feeling as heavy as a charcoal would. Please speak to us about suitable applications and any limitations before ordering.

name: Black Smooth
description: Deep black with a clean smooth face, sharp and graphic without surface texture to soften it. The wall reads as a single dark plane, which is precisely the point on contemporary buildings where the brickwork is meant to be architectural rather than rustic. Trial a panel before committing, since mortar colour changes dark brickwork more dramatically than any other choice you will make.

name: Light Weathered
description: Pale buffs and soft yellows under gentle darkened weathering, combining brightness with an aged quality. The lighter base keeps an elevation open while the weathering stops it looking new, which is a useful combination on extensions to older pale brickwork. Splashback at ground level is worth detailing out, since it shows on a pale brick far sooner than a dark one.

name: Cardinal Red Multi
description: Deep, rich reds with darker tones blended through, named for the ecclesiastical scarlet it echoes. It carries more weight and formality than an everyday red multi, which suits urban housing, apartment schemes and elevations meant to feel considered. It also does strong work as a darker banding course against a lighter brick.

name: Hadley Brindle
description: Streaked, mottled colouring is what brindling means, with darker tones running across a warm red-brown base. The effect gives a wall genuine surface interest and a hard-wearing traditional look without the weight of a full antique brick. Suits period extensions and elevations wanting character without the commitment of a heavily weathered brick.

name: Old Croft Blend
description: Worn reds and browns blended broadly over an irregular face, drawing on the modest brickwork of old crofts and smallholdings. The spread between bricks is wide, so a wall comes out looking accumulated over time rather than specified in one go. A soft lime mortar and a struck joint get you closer to the period look than the brick choice alone.

name: Weathered Orange
description: Warm terracotta orange under darkened, patchy weathering, combining sunlit colour with an aged surface. The weathering knocks back the brightness enough to let new brickwork sit beside something older without drawing attention to the join. On a north-facing elevation much of the warmth is lost, so orientation deserves a thought.

name: Brodsworth Mixture
description: Warm reds blended with browns and the occasional darker brick, giving an elevation depth and a solid Yorkshire character. Broad enough to hold interest across a large area, consistent enough to specify with confidence on a full development. Forgiving about mortar and straightforward to lay in volume.

name: KR77 Pale Red
description: A soft, light red with none of the depth of a conventional facing red. The paleness keeps it gentle rather than assertive, which suits situations where a red tone is wanted without the wall taking on the weight that a full red brings. Please speak to us about suitable applications and any limitations before ordering.

name: Weathered Red Stock
description: The creased, irregular face of traditional stock production in a weathered red, with darker patches scattered through. Colouring and surface work together to give a wall the settled quality of established brickwork rather than something newly delivered. A natural fit for period extensions, repairs and garden walls in established red brick streets.

name: Rural Multi
description: Reds, browns and softer buff tones blended into a brick with unhurried countryside character. No two faces are alike, so walls build up with the gentle mottling of farmhouses and village cottages. Made in the standard metric height and a 68mm imperial for older coursing.

name: Kingston Weathered Gault
description: Gault clay fires pale rather than red, giving the creams and soft yellows of eastern England, and here that pale base carries darkened weathering across the face. The result reads as gault brickwork that has been standing a good while rather than newly laid. Useful on London and East Anglian extensions where the existing stock is pale rather than red.

name: Mayfair Yellow Multi
description: Warm yellows blended with buff and softer brown tones, carrying the polished quality the name implies. Bright enough to lift an elevation, varied enough to look established, and a natural fit for extensions and infill in London's yellow brick districts. Check the coursing on the original wall before ordering, since older London housing rarely runs to modern gauge.

name: Chapel Blend
description: Reds and browns blended with softer weathered tones, carrying the plain dignity of nonconformist chapel brickwork. Variation is present but controlled, giving an elevation depth without the rustic looseness of a village multi. Equally comfortable on a new build, an extension or a run of boundary wall.

name: Brooklands Blend
description: Reds and browns blended with softer neutral tones over a lightly worked face. The variation is gentle rather than dramatic, making it easy to pair with whatever else is happening across the elevation, from render to timber to stone. Suits housing, extensions and garden walls where the brickwork is meant to support rather than lead.

name: Compton Weathered
description: Reds and browns under a darkened, softly weathered face, so new brickwork looks settled from the day it is pointed rather than freshly delivered. It suits extensions, repairs and garden walls where the job is to blend into what is already standing. A soft lime-toned mortar reinforces the aged quality; crisp grey pointing works against it.

name: KR75 Dark Grey
description: A deep charcoal grey, the darkest of the KR greys. It gives strong definition and a distinctly contemporary weight, working powerfully against pale render, glazing and light timber where a bold contrast is wanted. Please speak to us about suitable applications and any limitations before ordering.

name: York Red
description: A warm northern red with soft variation and a faintly grained face, solid and unpretentious in the way Yorkshire brickwork tends to be. It gives an elevation warmth and depth and then gets on with the business of being a wall. Forgiving on mortar, straightforward to lay, and consistent enough to order in quantity.

name: Park Royal
description: Warm reds and browns blended with a composed, urban quality, named for the west London district. Variation is restrained enough to specify across whole elevations without the wall becoming the loudest thing on the site, which suits apartment schemes and city infill. Forgiving on mortar and consistent enough to order in quantity across a large scheme.

name: Wrekin Berkshire Red
description: A mellow red with soft variation and a lightly worked face, warm rather than hard-edged. It settles beside period brickwork without fuss, which is why bricks of this character appear so often on extensions to older houses in the south. A soft lime-toned mortar and a struck joint will get you closer to a period match than the brick alone ever does.

name: Admiral Red Multi
description: Warm reds worked through with browns and darker mottling, giving an elevation depth without heavy contrast. A dependable everyday multi, forgiving about mortar choice and consistent enough to order in quantity for a full development or a single extension. A safe specification where dependability matters more than making a statement.

name: Richmond Blend
description: Reds and browns blended with softer neutral tones over a lightly worked face, composed rather than rustic. It gives an elevation depth without becoming a feature, which suits urban extensions and infill where the detailing is meant to lead. Forgiving on mortar and comfortable across whole elevations without becoming tiring.

name: Hurstwood Multi
description: Warm reds blended with browns and softer tones over a lightly worked face, giving quiet depth across an elevation. Nothing about it demands attention, which makes it a sensible default when the brickwork needs to support the building rather than define it. Works at any scale from a garden wall upwards.

name: Autumn Red
description: Warm reds with brown and amber running through, borrowing the colouring of the season it is named for. It reads mellow rather than bright, holding its warmth in flat light where more strident reds tend to go grey. Good across housing, extensions and garden walls where warmth matters more than uniformity.

name: Traditional English Red
description: Warm reds and browns over a lightly weathered, softly irregular face, giving the settled character of an established English wall. It is a dependable choice for period extensions, repairs and infill where a crisp modern brick would sit awkwardly against the original. Compare a sample against the existing wall in daylight, and check the coursing while you have the tape out.

name: Drayton Cream
description: Soft cream with gentle variation, bringing lightness and a little warmth to an elevation without the coldness of a grey or the flatness of a white. It works particularly well where stone and render set the tone rather than red brick. A dark mortar against it makes a strong graphic wall, which suits modern work particularly well.

name: Corum
description: Restrained colouring with subtle movement and a clean face, contemporary and composed. It gives an elevation a quiet, considered quality that suits modern architecture, and pairs cleanly with glazing, dark frames and timber. Suits contemporary housing, apartment schemes and elevations where restraint is the point.

name: Crigglestone Red
description: A warm Yorkshire red with gentle variation and a faintly grained face, unfussy and dependable. It gives an elevation consistency and warmth in equal measure, which makes it a safe specification across housing, extensions and boundary walls. Undemanding about mortar and easy to lay, which counts on a large job.

name: Heather Sandfaced
description: Heather colouring in soft purples and browns, finished with a fine sand-textured face that scatters light rather than reflecting it. The matt surface reads as traditional and understated, and helps new work settle beside older brickwork. Metric and 73mm imperial heights available. A soft lime-toned mortar suits it particularly well on period matching work.

name: Snowie Heritage Smooth
description: A clean smooth face with heritage colouring, bridging crisp modern brickwork and traditional tones. The even surface keeps lines sharp while the colour keeps the wall warm, a useful combination on contemporary extensions to older buildings. Metric and 73mm imperial heights available. Expect a consistent overall appearance with subtle movement rather than the variation of a strong multi.

name: Jubilee
description: Warm reds and browns blended with a celebratory richness, deeper and more generous than an everyday facing brick. It gives an elevation real presence, working well on substantial houses and schemes where the brickwork is intended to carry the building. Best given room to work across a full elevation rather than competing with other strong materials.

name: Lindfield Yellow Multi
description: Warm yellows blended with buff and softer brown tones, bright enough to lift an elevation and varied enough to look established rather than newly delivered. A sensible option for Sussex extensions and infill where the local stock runs yellow. Distribute the paler bricks evenly, since a cluster of light bricks is far more visible than a cluster of dark ones.

name: Alexia
description: Soft warm tones with gentle variation across the face, understated rather than assertive. It gives an elevation quiet depth and pairs easily with most materials, which makes it a comfortable choice where the brickwork is deliberately not the story. Forgiving on mortar and easy to pair with render, timber or stone.

name: Autumn Tint
description: Warm reds and browns with amber running through, soft rather than strong. The autumnal colouring lifts noticeably in low sun without the intensity of a full orange, which makes it easier to live with over a large elevation than a bolder warm brick. Good for extensions, garden walls and housing where a cooler brick would feel wrong.

name: Hampshire Stock Red Multi ATR
description: A red stock multi in the Hampshire tradition, with the creased irregular face of traditional stock production and reds and browns blended across it. The combination gives a wall the settled, weathered quality that suits period extensions and southern village work. Hold a sample against your own brickwork in daylight before ordering, as stock walls vary street by street.

name: Bivio
description: Warm tones blended with softer neutrals and a lightly worked face, contemporary in feel without being cold. It works as comfortably on a modern house as on an extension to something older, which is more than many bricks in this territory manage. Pairs cleanly with glazing, dark frames and timber cladding on contemporary schemes.

name: Flemish Antique
description: Darkened, patchy weathering over warm reds and browns, with the irregular face of continental brickwork that has stood for generations. It suits period extensions, conservation work and elevations laid in traditional bonds, where the brick needs to look as old as the pattern. A soft lime-toned mortar reinforces the aged appearance considerably.

name: Crigglestone Brown
description: Warm brown with red running through to keep it from going muddy, sitting in useful ground between the neutrality of grey and the commitment of a full red. It pairs particularly well with timber and stone, and gives a long elevation depth without shouting. A sensible option where the brickwork needs to recede and let another material lead.

name: Blenheim Red Multi
description: Warm reds worked through with browns and darker mottling, carrying a slightly grander quality than an everyday multi. It gives large elevations depth and presence, which suits substantial houses and schemes where the brickwork is meant to feel considered. Mix from three or four packs at once so the darker bricks spread evenly rather than gathering in one bay.

name: Heather Rustic
description: Purples and browns softening a red base, finished with a roughened rustic face. Colour and texture working together give a wall considerable depth, which suits period extensions and elevations wanting character without heavy weathering. Keep the face clean as you lay, since a rough surface holds mortar splashes more readily than a smooth one.

name: Ripley Rustic
description: A warm red with a roughened, textured face that throws shadow across an elevation and stops the colour reading as flat. Traditional in feel without going as far as an antique, which makes it a practical middle ground for housing, extensions and garden walls. Good across whole elevations, garden walls and anywhere a plain smooth red would feel too clean.

name: Danehill Yellow
description: A soft warm yellow with gentle variation, carrying the traditional brightness of Sussex and Wealden yellow brickwork. Straightforward for extensions and infill in yellow brick areas, where a red would look plainly imported into the street. It sits comfortably beside genuine stock brick without trying to imitate it, which is often what an extension needs.

name: Wickford
description: Warm reds and browns blended with softer tones over a lightly worked face, straightforward and undemanding. It gives an elevation quiet depth and pairs easily with most materials, which makes it a sensible default across housing, extensions and garden walls. Straightforward to lay and undemanding about what you put next to it.

name: Old Farmhouse
description: Worn reds and browns under gentle weathering, with the irregular face of brickwork that has stood on an exposed farm building for a century. It suits barn conversions, rural extensions and garden structures where anything crisp would look plainly imported. A soft lime mortar with a struck joint reinforces the weathered quality; crisp grey pointing undoes it.

name: Maltings
description: Warm reds and browns over a worn, softly irregular face, recalling the brickwork of old maltings and industrial buildings. The character is honest and hard-working rather than decorative, which suits conversions, urban infill and extensions to older commercial property. Also worth considering for internal exposed brickwork, where the industrial character reads particularly well.

name: Ledbury
description: Warm reds and browns with softer tones blended through, drawing on the mellow brickwork of the Welsh borders. The variation is gentle and the character settled, making it a comfortable option for rural extensions and market town infill. Comfortable on a new build, an extension or a run of garden wall.

name: Majestic
description: Deep, richly toned reds and browns with real weight to them, living up to a name that does not undersell itself. It gives large elevations presence and formality, which suits apartment schemes, civic work and houses wanting a considered palette. Grey mortar keeps it restrained; a pale joint throws the bond pattern into sharp relief.
